# Crawler Requirements-Quality Checklist: Stack Overflow Transaction Data Collector

**Purpose**: Validate the completeness, clarity, consistency, and measurability of requirements governing the crawler's core behaviours — transaction definition, tag filtering, ID uniqueness, pagination, date partitioning, resume, idempotency, output format, and scale target.
**Created**: 2026-09-26
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) · [data-model.md](../data-model.md) · [contracts/cli-contract.md](../contracts/cli-contract.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

---

## Transaction Definition

- [ ] CHK001 - Is the mapping from a Stack Overflow question to a transaction explicitly stated as a one-to-one relationship — i.e., exactly one question produces at most one transaction? [Completeness, Spec §Key Entities]
- [ ] CHK002 - Is `question_id` unambiguously identified as the sole transaction identifier, with no alternative or composite key permitted? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003]
- [ ] CHK003 - Is "items of a transaction" explicitly defined as the `tags` field of the question, with no other fields treated as transaction items? [Clarity, Spec §Key Entities]
- [ ] CHK004 - Is it clear whether a transaction represents the question at crawl time (snapshot) or whether it could be updated if the question is re-encountered? [Clarity, Gap]
- [ ] CHK005 - Are the optional context fields (`title`, `score`, `answer_count`, `creation_date`) distinguished from the core transaction fields (`question_id`, `tags`) in the requirements? [Completeness, Spec §Key Entities]

---

## ≥2 Tag Filtering

- [ ] CHK006 - Is the ≥2 tag threshold unambiguously applied to **distinct** tags (after deduplication within the question) rather than the raw tag count returned by the API? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK007 - Is it specified that tag deduplication occurs **before** the ≥2 count check — i.e., the order of operations is defined in the requirements? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK008 - Is "silently dropped" defined precisely enough to be testable — i.e., is it clear what log output (if any) should appear when a question is dropped for insufficient tags? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002, FR-007]
- [ ] CHK009 - Is the behaviour for a question with exactly 0 tags explicitly covered, or does the ≥2 rule implicitly subsume it without ambiguity? [Coverage, Spec §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK010 - Are the requirements consistent between the pipeline section (TagValidationPipeline drops items with < 2 tags) and the spec (≥2 distinct tags required), with no off-by-one ambiguity? [Consistency, Spec §FR-002, Data Model §Validation Rules]

---

## question_id Uniqueness

- [ ] CHK011 - Is the uniqueness guarantee for `question_id` stated as an invariant of the **output file** (not just a single run), meaning it must hold across all runs and restarts? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003, FR-006]
- [ ] CHK012 - Is the deduplication scope clearly bounded — i.e., is it clear that deduplication applies across the full history of the output file, not just within the current crawl session? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK013 - Is there a specified behaviour when a `question_id` collision is detected during a run — i.e., is the duplicate silently dropped or does it trigger a warning log? [Clarity, Gap]
- [ ] CHK014 - Is the type of `question_id` (integer) consistently specified across the spec, data model, and contract, with no ambiguity about string vs numeric representation in the output JSON? [Consistency, Data Model §Transaction, Spec §Key Entities]
- [ ] CHK015 - Is the requirement that the post-run validation utility reports duplicate `question_id` count (not just "yes/no") stated as a measurable acceptance criterion? [Measurability, Spec §FR-012, SC-001]

---

## Pagination Completeness

- [ ] CHK016 - Is the pagination termination condition fully specified — i.e., are all three signals defined (empty `items` array, `has_more: false`, page = 25 hard limit)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-017, research.md §D-004]
- [ ] CHK017 - Is the maximum pages-per-partition limit (25) stated as a hard constraint with a defined behaviour when reached — i.e., does the system treat it as end-of-partition and advance? [Clarity, Spec §FR-017, research.md §D-004]
- [ ] CHK018 - Is the per-page log entry requirement (page number, cumulative fetched, written, dropped) complete enough that a reviewer can verify pagination is advancing without inspecting the output file? [Measurability, Spec §FR-007, SC-003]
- [ ] CHK019 - Are the requirements for handling the API's `backoff` field (courtesy throttle signal) specified, or is this gap intentionally deferred? [Coverage, Gap]
- [ ] CHK020 - Is it specified whether pages within a partition are fetched in ascending or descending order, and whether this order matters for the deduplication or output ordering requirements? [Clarity, Gap]

---

## Date Partition Boundaries

- [ ] CHK021 - Is the 7-day partition window defined with a clear boundary rule — specifically, is `fromdate` inclusive and `todate` exclusive, so partitions do not overlap? [Clarity, Spec §Clarifications, research.md §D-002]
- [ ] CHK022 - Is the configurable start date (`PARTITION_START_DATE`) and end date (`PARTITION_END_DATE`) documented with a defined default and format (ISO-8601 date string)? [Completeness, contracts/cli-contract.md §Key Settings]
- [ ] CHK023 - Is it specified what happens when a partition produces zero questions — i.e., is an all-empty partition treated identically to a mid-partition empty page, and does it advance without error? [Coverage, Spec §FR-017]
- [ ] CHK024 - Is the partition advancement logic (moving from one 7-day window to the next) testable independently — i.e., can a reviewer verify it by running a single-partition crawl and confirming the spider does not request a second partition? [Measurability, quickstart.md §Stage 1]
- [ ] CHK025 - Is there a requirement specifying the behaviour when `PARTITION_END_DATE` falls mid-week — i.e., is the final partition truncated to the end date, or is it always a full 7-day window? [Clarity, Gap]

---

## Resume Behaviour

- [ ] CHK026 - Is the resume entry point specified with enough precision to be tested — i.e., is it clear that the spider resumes from the exact page and partition where it was interrupted, not just from the start of the interrupted partition? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005, Data Model §CrawlCheckpoint]
- [ ] CHK027 - Is the JOBDIR mechanism identified as the sole checkpoint strategy, and is it specified that the JOBDIR path must remain consistent between the interrupted run and the resumed run for resumption to work? [Completeness, Spec §Assumptions, research.md §D-005]
- [ ] CHK028 - Is there a requirement specifying the behaviour when the JOBDIR is missing or corrupted at restart time — i.e., does the spider start over or fail fast with a clear error? [Coverage, Gap]
- [ ] CHK029 - Is the relationship between JOBDIR state and output file state specified at the resume boundary — i.e., are there requirements for what happens if JOBDIR indicates page N of partition X, but the output file contains records from page N+1? [Clarity, Spec §FR-014, Clarifications Q2]
- [ ] CHK030 - Is the progress log's "total_written" counter defined as reflecting only the current run, or the cumulative count across all runs including records written before the resume? [Clarity, Spec §FR-007, contracts/cli-contract.md §Progress Logging]

---

## Cross-Run Idempotency

- [ ] CHK031 - Is idempotency defined precisely: running the same crawl command twice (with an already-complete output file) produces no change to the output file? [Completeness, Spec §FR-015]
- [ ] CHK032 - Is the startup distinct-ID count check (FR-015) specified as occurring **before** any API requests, ensuring zero quota is consumed when the target is already met? [Clarity, Spec §FR-015, SC-007]
- [ ] CHK033 - Is there a specified requirement for what constitutes a "valid" line during the startup scan — i.e., are malformed JSON lines counted, skipped, or flagged? [Clarity, Spec §FR-014]
- [ ] CHK034 - Is the cross-run deduplication strategy (output file as source of truth) specified as the authoritative mechanism, with no secondary deduplication store required? [Clarity, Spec §Assumptions, research.md §D-007]
- [ ] CHK035 - Is it specified that re-running after quota exhaustion (partial run) produces no duplicate records in the output — i.e., is cross-run idempotency explicitly required for the quota-halt-and-resume scenario? [Completeness, Spec §FR-016, Clarifications Q4]

---

## JSON Output Validity

- [ ] CHK036 - Is the output format specified as NDJSON (one JSON object per line) with the exact file extension (`.jsonl`) documented? [Clarity, Spec §Assumptions, research.md §D-008]
- [ ] CHK037 - Is the schema of each output record (fields, types, formats) fully specified — specifically, is the `creation_date` ISO-8601 format and the `tags` array element type (string) unambiguous? [Completeness, Data Model §Transaction]
- [ ] CHK038 - Is there a requirement specifying the encoding of the output file (UTF-8) so that non-ASCII characters in tag names or titles do not produce invalid JSON? [Coverage, Gap]
- [ ] CHK039 - Is the behaviour defined for the StoragePipeline when a write to the output file fails mid-append — i.e., are there requirements preventing a partial line from being written? [Coverage, Gap]
- [ ] CHK040 - Is the validation utility's output format specified clearly enough that its results can be used as an automated gate — i.e., are exit codes and reported metrics defined? [Measurability, Spec §FR-012, contracts/cli-contract.md §Validation Utility]
- [ ] CHK041 - Are requirements consistent between the spec (final output is "JSON") and the data model/contract (NDJSON / JSON Lines), or is the distinction explicitly acknowledged? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004, research.md §D-008]

---

## 100k Valid Transaction Target

- [ ] CHK042 - Is "100,000 valid unique transactions" defined with sufficient precision — i.e., does the requirement explicitly state that the count is of **distinct question_ids**, not total output lines? [Clarity, Spec §SC-001, FR-015]
- [ ] CHK043 - Is the target stated as a minimum (≥ 100,000) rather than an exact value, and is there a requirement for what happens if the collector overshoots (e.g., stops at 100,001)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-010, FR-015]
- [ ] CHK044 - Is the success criterion SC-001 measurable by the validation utility alone, without requiring manual inspection of the output file? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001, FR-012]
- [ ] CHK045 - Is it specified that the 100k target is cumulative across all runs (not per-run), allowing it to be reached across multiple quota-bounded sessions? [Completeness, Spec §FR-010, Clarifications Q4]
- [ ] CHK046 - Is there a requirement stating the behaviour when the target is exceeded — e.g., the crawler collects 102,000 records before it detects the threshold? Is over-collection acceptable? [Clarity, Gap]
- [ ] CHK047 - Are the three crawl stages (pilot ≤ 500, small-batch ≤ 5,000, full-scale 100k+) specified with explicit gate criteria — i.e., is it documented what evidence is required to advance from Stage 1 to Stage 2, and from Stage 2 to Stage 3? [Completeness, Spec §Assumptions, quickstart.md §Stage 1–3]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after reviewer confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or further review.
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`; do not modify it here.
- Items marked `[Gap]` indicate requirements that are missing from the current spec and may warrant a spec update before implementation begins.
- Items marked `[Ambiguity]` indicate terms or conditions that are present but not yet quantified or clarified.
